test_cases.question: What is the default voting threshold for Board decisions?
test_cases.answer: The Board shall take decisions by a simple majority of its members, unless otherwise provided for in this Regulation. This means most decisions require only more than half of the members to agree.
test_cases.supporting_quote: The Board shall take decisions by a simple majority of its members, unless otherwise provided for in this Regulation

test_cases.question: What voting threshold is required for the Board to adopt its rules of procedure?
test_cases.answer: The Board shall adopt its own rules of procedure by a two-thirds majority of its members. This is higher than the simple majority required for most other decisions.
test_cases.supporting_quote: The Board shall adopt its own rules of procedure by a two-thirds majority of its members

test_cases.question: Can the Board establish its own internal working methods?
test_cases.answer: Yes. The Board has autonomy to organise its own operational arrangements. This means the Board can determine its internal working methods, processes, and structures without external prescription.

coverage.72(1): Test case 1 - Simple majority default + exception clause
coverage.72(2) rules: Test case 2 - Two-thirds majority for rules of procedure
coverage.72(2) operations: Test case 3 - Organise own operational arrangements

b2b_relevance: LOW - Article 72 is purely about EDPB internal governance. No direct business obligations. However, understanding voting thresholds helps explain why some EDPB decisions take longer (binding decisions under Art 65 require 2/3 majority, not simple majority).
